description:
📝 Notes
Feb 24, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes reviewed the website, with Gabor Kerekes agreeing to remove blog posts and address a broken link, and Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh then worked to grant Gabor Kerekes, Amir Houieh, and Noémi Biró necessary G-Cloud permissions to run analytics scripts for Melissa. Amir Houieh updated the Nexus to include persistent memory with two storage types and plans to create use cases using real data, while Noémi Biró suggested adding content to the homepage to highlight the "body research division." Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh also discussed their competitive analysis of UNMS, strategic outreach methods, and the conceptualization of their system as a personal OS with an AI kernel integrated with Nexus.
Details
Website Review and Adjustments: Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes reviewed the website design, and Gabor Kerekes noted that they would remove a few blog posts and address a repeated paragraph (00:00:00). They also identified a broken link. Noémi Biró suggested that the homepage felt underwhelming and recommended adding a line about the current focus on the "body research division" similar to what is on the lab page to direct attention. Gabor Kerekes acknowledged the suggestion and mentioned they were satisfied with the current typography and spacing (00:03:02).
Homepage Content and Interaction: The team discussed adding a short sentence or animation to the homepage to indicate the current focus, such as a "currently focusing on" line or an animation that shows what the organization is about. Noémi Biró suggested that if an animation is used, it should function as a link to the lab page so users know it is clickable (00:05:31). Gabor Kerekes mentioned they would push the current site changes and then work on figuring out how to apply configured tiles which currently do not apply when the site is built. Gabor Kerekes planned to push the changes after the meeting (00:06:56).
G-Cloud Permissions Refactoring and Testing: Gabor Kerekes refactored the permissions on G-Cloud, giving Amir Houieh permissions similar to their own, including the ability to change the infrastructure, and giving Noémi Biró enough permissions to run the analytics script (00:06:56). The primary goal was to test if both Amir Houieh and Noémi Biró had access to the analytics and could run the relevant scripts. Noémi Biró noted they would need the analytics export for Melissa, and Gabor Kerekes shared the necessary instructions (00:08:49).
Troubleshooting Analytics Script Access: Amir Houieh attempted to run the analytics script and encountered a warning about application default login and a subsequent error stating that the "Tunnel failed to become ready within 10 seconds". Noémi Biró also sought clarification on the steps to run the script and received the instructions (00:10:20). Gabor Kerekes confirmed that the script was running and advised to let it continue, stating they would debug the errors after the meeting (00:16:25). Gabor Kerekes emphasized the difficulty in testing due to their own account having too many privileges and the intent to give user accounts only necessary, minimal privileges (00:18:34).
Nexus Development Update: Amir Houieh reported that they worked on the Nexus, which now includes persistent memory supporting two types of storage: one in memory for testing and one supporting SQL light using the embedded better SQL light 3 version for NodeJS. Amir Houieh plans to push the update soon and wants to create at least one or two use cases for Nexus this week to run it with real data, potentially using a chat with Claude (00:20:08). Amir Houieh considered using the Nexus to learn about their browser history, reading topics, and shopping behavior (00:21:27).
Competitive Analysis and Inspiration: Gabor Kerekes shared information about UNMS, a company making apps similar to their ideas, which they posted about in the R&D channel as competition. They detailed one of UNMS's products, which acts as a chat interface and bookmarking tool that generates insights and connections between saved content and conversations using agents (00:21:27). Amir Houieh and Gabor Kerekes agreed they could improve upon this concept, noting their different origin and assumptions (00:23:09).
Hardware Design and Inspiration: Amir Houieh shared a website about a type of computer for experts, appreciating its branding and hardware design, particularly the keyboard (00:24:30). Gabor Kerekes also shared a link to another hardware product, a cool-looking dial, suggesting they need a bookmarking tool to share such links easily. Gabor Kerekes confirmed they are designing a bookmarking tool and are working on the specifications (00:26:36).
Transition to Core Discussion: Noémi Biró interrupted the ongoing conversation to confirm that the updated analytics had been sent to Melissa, which Gabor Kerekes confirmed they had sent to the Cibil channel. Noémi Biró confirmed they would send the file to Melissa now. Gabor Kerekes suggested continuing the meeting and showed another inspirational product, Mainframe, a company whose landing page and connection to key figures in Figma they appreciated (00:29:54).
Strategy for Outreach and Visibility: The team discussed the difficulty of reaching key figures in the industry, such as the former Figma figure and the Daylight Computing founder (00:31:26). Gabor Kerekes stressed that outreach must be calculated and impressive to capture attention within a three-second window. Amir Houieh suggested the best approach would be to gain enough visibility so their work naturally falls under the radar of influential people (00:33:01).
Conceptualizing the AI Kernel/Personal OS: Gabor Kerekes presented a visualization and metaphor of what they are building as a personal Operating System (OS) with an AI kernel (00:33:01). The applications are seen as portals to interact with this kernel, which consists of long-term memory, agents, and the Nexus, building an understanding of the user and acting as a data repository. Gabor Kerekes likened the kernel to the low-level layer of a traditional OS that translates user-level applications into hardware instructions (00:35:35).
Use Cases for the AI Kernel and Nexus: Gabor Kerekes provided use case examples for the AI kernel/Nexus, such as a bookmarking app interacting with the kernel to notice patterns, like security issues, and subsequently provide a personalized digest of relevant saved articles. Another example involves the kernel processing personal conversations or journaling about topics like ADHD and connecting them to other saved notes (00:37:52). The system is intended to act proactively, potentially noticing lack of sleep and suggesting suitable to-dos based on energy levels without the user having to express tiredness (00:40:06).
Suggested next steps
Amir Houieh will push the Nexus updates with the SQL light storage today.
Amir Houieh will make at least one or two use cases of Nexus to run with real data this week.
Gabor Kerekes will remove a few blog posts from the website and push the recent changes to the website, figuring out how to apply the configured tiles.
Noémi Biró will send the updated analytics to Melissa.
Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh will debug the error Amir Houieh received after the meeting.
